author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A man accused in a May shooting along Memorial Drive in Cambridge is expected to appear in court in person for the first time while facing dozens of newly filed charges.

WHDH identified the defendant as 47-year-old Tyler Brown. The station reported that the new counts include six charges of armed assault to murder, seven charges of malicious damage to a motor vehicle, carrying a firearm without a license and possessing a firearm after a felony conviction.

Prosecutors allege Brown fired dozens of rounds from a rifle at drivers along Memorial Drive. Two people were struck and later recovered. Brown’s earlier court appearance took place by video from a hospital bed, according to the report.

The charges are allegations, and Brown is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. His upcoming appearance advances a case that has been developing for nearly four months and will allow the court to address the expanded charging document. WHDH also reported that Brown was on parole at the time in connection with a 2020 shooting involving Boston police officers. Any plea, bail decision or schedule for further proceedings will be determined in court.
dek: Tyler Brown is expected to appear in person as prosecutors add armed-assault, firearm and property-damage counts tied to the May shooting.
headline: Memorial Drive shooting suspect faces dozens of new charges
